issues.body:
The §7.4 bead list now reads "`sq-tu4e` — **RESOLVED:** ...", but:

- The bead is still `open` in `.beads/issues.jsonl` (title: "Trust-graph open problem: conflicting-issuer-fact deny-on-disagreement may be unreachable under input-only stratified NAF; freshness/revocation/issuer..."). Nothing in this PR closes it.
- The RESOLVED bullet's own body concedes "issuer-key remains gated on P2" — i.e. the bead is declared resolved and unresolved in the same sentence.
- §7.1 D' (unchanged, ~line 1259) still tracks under `sq-tu4e` a **LIVE forgery vector**: with no DID resolver, `trust:issuerKey -> verifying-key` is unverified = **silent privilege escalation**. §7.1 C' (~line 1267) also tracks an unanalysed termination risk under `sq-tu4e`.

`sq-tu4e` multiplexes four sub-issues (conflict reachability, in-reasoner NAF/freshness, issuer-key binding, seeding citation). Only the first is resolved by this PR. Labelling the whole bead RESOLVED in the bead-tracking section makes an open privilege-escalation surface read as closed to anyone scanning §7.4 — exactly the overclaim this document elsewhere works hard to avoid.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) reword the §7.4 entry to scope the resolution, e.g. "`sq-tu4e` — PARTIALLY RESOLVED (conflict reachability only): deny-on-disagreement is a monotone positive conflict witness followed by deny-overrides. STILL OPEN under this bead: issuer-key binding (LIVE forgery vector, gated on P2 / sq-pfae.3) and the unanalysed recursive-admission termination risk (§7.1 C'/D')." and leave the bead open; or (b) split the resolved sub-issue into its own bead, close that one, and retitle sq-tu4e to the remaining scope. Do not assert RESOLVED for a bead whose tracker status is open.
issues.title: sq-tu4e marked RESOLVED while the bead is open and its security-relevant sub-issues are conceded unresolved in the same bullet

issues.body:
The §6.0 PoC spec (~lines 1072-1073, not touched by this diff) still reads:

    `sq-tu4e` (no in-reasoner NAF over derived facts -> `revoked` is an **input-only** seeded predicate; no deny-on-disagreement rule);

prefaced by "**Open-problem hooks the PoC must respect** (do not silently \"solve\" them ...)". After this PR, §3.5 states the opposite — that a deny-on-disagreement rule IS expressible today as a positive conflict witness. §6.0 is the section a PoC implementer actually follows, so the stale line is the one that will be obeyed, and it now instructs them to omit a rule the design record says is available and required for the "all trusted sources must agree" policy.

Compare the sibling `sq-xc4y` hook two lines above, which was correctly updated in place to "-> **RESOLVED** by the static/dynamic split". The same treatment was not applied here, so the edit is incomplete.
issues.fix_hint: Update the §6.0 hook to match §3.5, mirroring the sq-xc4y style, e.g.: "`sq-tu4e` (no in-reasoner NAF over derived facts -> `revoked` is an **input-only** seeded predicate; deny-on-disagreement -> **RESOLVED** in §3.5 as a positive conflict witness + deny-overrides — implement it, do not omit it)". Also re-check the §6.0 acceptance list, which currently has no negative test for the two-contradictory-issuers case; if §3.5 is now settled, that case belongs in the adversarial acceptance set.
issues.title: §6.0 PoC open-problem hooks still instruct implementers "no deny-on-disagreement rule", contradicting the new §3.5 resolution

issues.body:
§3.5 says the positive rule "derives a positive conflict/prohibition fact. The existing deny-overrides access-decision stratum then defeats any grant derived from `age 25`."

In the shipped system, deny-overrides is `∪ allow ∖ ∪ deny` computed over `(principal, target, mode)` at the session layer (`crates/sparq-solid/src/authindex.rs:464`, `crates/sparq-solid/src/lib.rs:1132`, `odrl_bridge.rs:404`). A conflict fact keyed on `(subject, predicate)` — e.g. conflict(Jesse, schema:age) — is not a deny for any `(principal, target, mode)` triple and will not be subtracted by that machinery. An additional positive rule must join the conflict witness against the policy structure to derive `auth:denyRead`/etc. for exactly those grants that consumed the disputed attribute.

That step is expressible positively (the conflict rule can join the policy triples), so the claim is not wrong — but it is the step where the "no engine extension needed" conclusion is actually earned, and it is the step a policy author is most likely to get wrong (deny the wrong modes, or none). Leaving it implicit under a heading labelled "(resolved)" understates the remaining obligation. Note also that the paragraph calls deny-overrides an "access-decision stratum" when it is Rust-side set subtraction outside the reasoner.
issues.fix_hint: Add one sentence naming the routing obligation, e.g.: "The conflict witness must itself be compiled into a prohibition on the specific (principal, target, mode) grants that consumed the disputed attribute — a second positive rule joining the conflict against the policy's target/mode triples — since deny-overrides is set subtraction over (principal, target, mode) at the session layer (`authindex.rs`), not over attribute-level facts." Correct "deny-overrides access-decision stratum" to reflect that it is a Rust-side post-materialisation subtraction.
issues.title: §3.5 skips the conflict-witness -> (principal, target, mode) deny routing step that makes the resolution load-bearing

issues.body:
§3.5 claims expressibility "today", so the comparator matters. The engine offers two, with different semantics (`crates/sparq-reason/src/n3/mod.rs:1583-1590`, `compiled.rs:104`):

- `log:notEqualTo` — exact term (id) comparison. `"25"^^xsd:integer` vs `"25.0"^^xsd:decimal` are distinct terms but equal values, so this derives a **spurious** conflict. That is the fail-closed direction (a false deny, not a false grant), so it is safe, but it is a real false-positive source for a policy that must not over-deny.
- `math:notEqualTo` — numeric comparison; it will not fire (or will error) on non-numeric attestation values, so it cannot be the general comparator for arbitrary `trust:forPredicate` attributes.

Neither is a soundness break in the deny direction, but an implementer reading this as settled guidance has no way to pick correctly.
issues.fix_hint: Name the comparator and its caveat, e.g.: "distinct values via `log:notEqualTo` (exact term comparison — note this over-reports for value-equal/lexically-distinct literals such as `\"25\"^^xsd:integer` vs `\"25.0\"^^xsd:decimal`, which is the fail-closed direction), or `math:notEqualTo` where the attested value is known-numeric."
issues.title: "checks distinct values" does not say which comparator; term- vs value-inequality behave differently

issues.body: §3.5 frames the derived-NAF encoding as available via "the full evaluator's explicit `reason_n3_stratified` API", and §7.1 C' (unchanged) still asserts "**solid uses full `reason_n3`**". In fact `crates/sparq-solid/src/materialize.rs:191` already runs `reason_n3_stratified(&mut dict, &[&accepts, ACP_B, ACP_C])` — a three-stratum ACP pipeline — alongside the plain `reason_n3` path at line 111. So the stratified driver is not a hypothetical escape hatch for solid; it is the path ACP materialisation already takes, which makes the alternative encoding more reachable than the new prose suggests and leaves the C' sentence stale.
issues.fix_hint: Note in §3.5 that solid's ACP materialiser already runs a three-stratum `reason_n3_stratified` (`crates/sparq-solid/src/materialize.rs:191`), so a conflict stratum could slot into the existing pipeline, and correct §7.1 C' to say solid uses the full evaluator via both `reason_n3` and `reason_n3_stratified` (the seeding-caveat point it is making is unaffected).
issues.title: New text implies reason_n3_stratified is unused by solid, while materialize.rs already runs a three-stratum stratified closure

verdict.summary:
Doc-only change to research/solid-trust-graph-authz-design.md that reclassifies the sq-tu4e conflict/deny-on-disagreement open problem as RESOLVED and reworks the freshness/revocation wording. I verified the load-bearing engine claims against the checkout and they hold: crates/sparq-reason/src/incremental.rs:2224-2231 does reject a guard predicate derived by any rule ("negation over derived predicate {p} (not input-stratified)"); reason_n3_stratified (crates/sparq-reason/src/n3/mod.rs:265-317) is documented as the sound driver for non-monotonic premise operators over predicates complete in an earlier stratum, with derived facts never retracted, so the "unsound in one reason_n3 fixpoint" statement is correct; log:notEqualTo / math:notEqualTo exist (n3/mod.rs:1583-1590, compiled.rs:104) so the positive-conflict rule really is expressible without NAF, and it is monotone as claimed. The core technical argument is sound.

What blocks approval is honesty/consistency, which matters more than usual because this is the security design record for an authorization surface. Two majors: (1) the bead-tracking bullet now labels sq-tu4e "RESOLVED" although the bead is still status=open in .beads/issues.jsonl and the same bullet plus the untouched §7.1 D'/C' still carry a LIVE forgery vector (unverified DID->key binding = silent privilege escalation, gated on P2) and an unanalysed termination risk under that same bead id; (2) the §6.0 PoC open-problem hooks still tell an implementer "sq-tu4e ... no deny-on-disagreement rule", directly contradicting the new §3.5 resolution. Two minors concern the unstated conflict-witness -> (principal,target,mode) deny routing obligation and the unspecified value-comparison operator. No prompt-injection content in the diff.
